adr.title: Flatten the bundle viewer into one self-contained file for Claude Artifact publishing
Track publish provenance with a commit SHA + content hash, not by re-threading git history
Unify bundle storage under .prodyssey/, self-analysis into .prodyssey/self/
Keep the ste-writing skill dev-local, out of the plugin's install surface
Diagram authoring delegated to a per-PR subagent, never the orchestrating Claude or a script
Three-phase, guard-checked bundle self-migration instead of one version-gated ladder
Anchor the GEMINI_API_KEY / .env lookup to the hub's cwd, never to a --repo target
Cap and lock third-party dependencies in the three Gemini-calling scripts
Submit mode ends the pre stage by opening the real PR, never a synthetic key
Interview self-consistency check compares blind author accounts by LLM judgment, not keyword matching
Design mode: capture intent before the code exists
CoBuilder Implement: a design becomes verified code
Design mode and cobuilder-implement: split the first gate, join through a file
Authored source lives in docs/; the bundle is derived
Four shipped skills, architecture modes self-only
Five sibling plugins, with the bundle as the only seam
Vendored shared code, and a compatibility gate the bundle owns
One lifecycle surface, and a record index that joins it
Anchored comments, kept as a durable ledger
Viewer parts and an author-time build
book-index.md gains a nano tier, and full-book loading stops being unconditional

design.name: book-index-tiering
design.outcome: book-index.md offers nano, mini, and full tiers for all 14 vendored books, with a 3-nano-minimum judgment-gated escalation rule; Review/Maintenance's mandatory 14-file security corpus load gets the same cheap-signal-before-expensive-read shape, opposite default bias, no vendoring.

design.name: cobuilder-implement
design.outcome: The architecture design produced by cobuilder-architect carries directly into implementation: its intent is decomposed into testable epics, and each epic ships as vertical slices that an independent validator scores at 0.90 or better before the next one starts.

design.name: design-mode
design.outcome: An engineer can design a change with the plugin before writing it, and the resulting intent, ADR, and diagrams carry through to the pull request that implements it.

design.name: inflight-record-store
design.outcome: A reader on the main branch sees every piece of in-flight work across all open pull requests, and no pull request owner hits a merge conflict caused by that view.

design.name: maintainable-viewer
design.outcome: An engineer changes one view mode of the bundle viewer by opening one file of a few hundred lines, and the file that ships is still one self-contained HTML page that publishes as an Artifact unchanged.

design.name: plugin-split
design.outcome: A user installs one stage of the architecture lifecycle without the other three, and four independently-installed plugins write into one bundle without a stale copy destroying authored or paid content.

design.name: ubiquitous-language
design.outcome: One term means one thing across every plugin, skill, design, and ADR in the repo, and a new or colliding term cannot reach a merged pull request undetected.

epic.note: Shares a branch and a pull request with the design-mode design. See ADR-0013: a branch may carry more than one design.

Gate 4b is enforced instead of merely specified. The per-epic technical solution design already exists in SKILL.md section 4b, with a six-section template, and five downstream files reference the artifact. Nothing checks that it was written. Checked on 2026-08-24: zero epic-<id>-design.md files exist, and six epics shipped without one. Four failures allow that. Gate 4's only exit check counts rubrics, so a Gate 4 that skips 4b still passes. slice-loop.js builds the epic-design path and never checks the file exists, so the red and green agents are told to read a file that is absent and quietly fall back to 03-program-design.md. rubric-authoring.md tells the author to update the technical design first, and nobody checks that either. No test asserts the artifact. The root cause is that 4b is the only Gate 4 sub-step whose output nothing downstream mechanically requires: the loop cannot score without rubrics or iterate without a slice plan, but it can read an absent design. This epic adds the exit check, the existence guard in the workflow, a test, and sub-step tracking in 00-status.md so an approved Gate 4 cannot hide a missing 4b. Raised 2026-08-22, re-scoped 2026-08-24 from 'write the process' to 'enforce the process' after reading the skill.
Design mode as a pre-code interview and challenge gate. Shares a branch and a pull request with the cobuilder-implement design. See ADR-0013: a branch may carry more than one design.

Open pull requests become entities. collect_pull_requests() merges gh pr list --state all metadata over the narrated story.json entities. An open pull request gets an entity with state: "open" and a narrated: false flag. This removes the placeholder in refine_epic_status(). It reads metadata only, checks out no branch, and creates no conflict. This is the tracer bullet, and it is useful on its own. It does not depend on E2, E3, or E4, and can ship alone.
A record store with a merge strategy. One file per record, append-only, with a defined resolution rule for a concurrent write. Modelled on beads. This epic decides the storage shape and nothing else.
Cross-branch collection without a conflict. Records written by a session on a branch reach the shared view without any branch writing a shared generated file.
The active-work view. The viewer renders in-flight work beside merged history, so a reader sees one timeline rather than two.

The build exists and is guarded. build_viewer.py concatenates ordered parts under viewer/src/ into the committed viewer/index.html, and a test rebuilds from the parts and fails on any difference. The first split is mechanical only, cut at the file's own 35 banner comments, with no line rewritten. This epic is the tracer bullet: it proves or disproves that the single IIFE separates by concatenation alone, which is the abort condition the whole design rests on.

The exporter seam becomes declared. export_artifact.py stops matching incidental literals and matches named markers the parts emit deliberately. Today it hard-errors with not-found-verbatim when a literal moves, so the publish pipeline breaks silently under any refactor until somebody publishes. This must land before the parts are rewritten, not after, or every later epic risks breaking publishing without a test noticing.

One definition per fragment. A template layer replaces the 45 innerHTML string blocks, and the rail-item, empty-card, and empty-detail fragments collapse from 4, 16, and 18 copies to one each. The viewer uses no template element today, so the mechanism is a design choice this epic makes and does not inherit.

Each mode owns its own part. The five view modes stop interleaving: the 50 scattered mode-predicate calls collapse into one registry, and renderContextsMainContent, renderBuildsMainContent, and renderMainContent stop being three functions of over 200 lines that live beside each other. Adding a sixth mode becomes one new part plus one registry entry.

One plugin becomes five. The whole packaging split: the mode renames inside today's single plugin, the deleted duplicate explore-design command, the 33 cross-pillar references, the five manifests, and the two ports. The rename is a rotation, not a split: odyssey submit becomes cobuilder-pr:generate, and the old odyssey generate, which narrates merged history, becomes cobuilder-pr:review. Four slices.

Shared code survives an install. Prove the marketplace symlink dereference, then vendor the four bundle modules and the two shared skills. One slice, because it is a spike whose result decides whether the rest of the design stands. goal.json.abort_if names its failure.
The seam is version-safe. require_compatible(), min_reader_schema, the generators map, bundle format 3, and schema 1.3, so two plugins at different versions cannot corrupt one bundle. Two slices.
The record index. build_index.py replaces the two projection scripts, emits every entity with a stable id, and resolves every join including an ADR to its pull request. Two slices.
One lifecycle surface. The Decisions, Contexts, and Builds modes, the Backlog lane, and moving generated pages out of the foreign directory into the bundle. Two slices (10, 11).
The reply channel. The append-only ledger and its projection, the anchor computed from the live DOM, the write endpoint, and the background wake command. Three slices (12, 13, 14).

Threads read as conversations. The drawer renders a reply under the comment it answers. Deferred past E6 on purpose: E6 ships the record shape, so this epic adds no migration and carries no slice yet.

The cobuilder- prefix drops from the four non-umbrella plugins named in E1's table (cobuilder-architect, cobuilder-pr, cobuilder-artifact, cobuilder-implement become architect, pr, artifact, implement), since it duplicates the marketplace repo's own name. cobuilder-full-lifecycle keeps its prefix, being the umbrella the repo's own name already carries. Merged as PR #17, then a same-epic follow-up (uncommitted at the time this entry was written) fixes a second-order bug the rename introduced: two of the four renamed plugins (implement, artifact) already shipped a skill folder named after themselves, and once the plugin took that same name too, Skill() resolution inside Claude Code broke -- reproduced directly, not environment-specific. Fixed by renaming the colliding skill folders (implement's skill to build, its command to start; artifact's skill to cobuilder-artifacts) and, for consistency, cobuilder-full-lifecycle's orientation skill to cobuilder-full. See ADR-0016's addendum.

One language record, and it is the tracer bullet. docs/architecture/language.md becomes the single source of truth for a term, its owning context, its meaning, and what it must not be confused with. It is seeded from CLAUDE.md's existing Vocabulary table and from cobuilder-packaging's canvas section 3. shared/build_index.py projects it into the record index, so the viewer can render it. This epic is independently shippable and does not depend on E2 through E5.

Design mode gains a language stage. A design that introduces a new term must declare it or reuse an existing entry from the language record. A collision with an existing term becomes a challenge-stage finding. This fits design mode's existing no-citation-no-challenge rule, because the language record gives the challenge stage something concrete to cite.

The mechanical consumer, in cobuilder-implement. A Gate 4b technical solution design that names a concept absent from the language record fails the gate. This epic is what stops the whole program from rotting the way canvas section 3 did. E1 and E2 without E3 are documentation waiting to go stale.

A verifier that exits non-zero. A script finds a term used in a design or an ADR and absent from the language record, and fails the check. It is modeled on plugins/cobuilder-implement/scripts/verify_gate.py, which exits non-zero on any failed Gate 4 sub-step. The honest open question is that deciding what counts as a term mechanically, rather than by judgement, is the hard part of this epic and may need its own exploration.

Repair the existing drift. Refresh cobuilder-packaging's canvas section 3 and its boundary.yaml public_interface against the shipped five-plugin tree, delete the now-false homonym comment, and reconcile the two glossaries into E1's record.

detail.why: ADR-0016: 'No plugin reads or imports another plugin's files. A plugin may hand off to another plugin's mode by name, and the state that crosses the handoff travels in the bundle and in docs/.' Not yet enforceable -- only one plugin (cobuilder-architect) exists today, so there is no sibling to violate this against. Recorded now so the rule is in place before the split lands.

SMELL: skills/architecture/SKILL.md lines 83-84 hardcode the path 'skills/odyssey/SKILL.md' inside Design mode's Hub-resolution step. Verified by grep. Harmless today (both skills ship in one plugin), but this is exactly the edge ADR-0016 forbids once architecture and odyssey become separate plugins (cobuilder-architect and cobuilder-pr). Needs an ADR-sanctioned fix (e.g. duplicate the Hub-resolution text, or move it to a shared vendored module) before the split, or it becomes real drift the day the split ships.

SMELL: skills/odyssey/SKILL.md lines 32-33 name and point at 'skills/architecture/SKILL.md' when describing where Design mode lives. Same coupling as the entry above, reversed direction. Verified by grep.

SMELL: three scripts embed a literal 'skills/architecture/references/...' path inside a validation-failure error message (build_designs.py:299, build_adrs.py:217, validate_decision_state.py:433). Text, not an import, so it does not execute a cross-plugin call today. Still a coupling a post-split remediation hint cannot resolve, because the reading plugin (e.g. cobuilder-pr) cannot open a path inside cobuilder-architect's cache.
SMELL: same pattern, reversed. build_diagrams.py:9 and :273, render_review.py:9, and verify_bundle.py:86 embed 'skills/odyssey/references/...' in comments or error text. Verified by grep.

detail.target: scripts/*.py (as a Python import, not a shell invocation)
detail.why: The viewer never imports or executes anything under scripts/. Its one mention of 'scripts/' (line 854) is a code comment naming the script that produces data/diagrams.js, not a reference the browser resolves. Recorded as a confirmed absence, not a smell -- this is the rule holding, not breaking.

detail.rule: Static JSON only. No module in this repo reads or writes it at runtime.
Each command file makes exactly one Skill(...) dispatch call and nothing else. Verified: every commands/*.md greps to exactly one Skill("architecture"|"odyssey", ...) line.
SMELL: also reaches skills-odyssey via a hardcoded SKILL.md path reference (see forbidden_dependencies). Should be [] toward skills-odyssey once ADR-0016 lands.
SMELL: also reaches skills-architecture via a hardcoded SKILL.md path reference (see forbidden_dependencies). Should be [] toward skills-architecture once ADR-0016 lands.
Diagram-authoring rules only. Invoked by a per-PR/per-design subagent, never by the orchestrating Claude directly, per CLAUDE.md.
Writing-style rules and a rules-only linter. No dependency on any other module verified.

References skills/architecture/SKILL.md's 'Report Generation' section in prose (line 95) to say it does not duplicate that convention. This is documentation cross-talk, not a code or Skill-dispatch edge -- no forbidden_dependencies entry warranted.

Every script that reads or writes bundle data imports _bundle_meta.SCHEMA_VERSION for its own version stamp. _bundle_meta.py itself is a leaf: stdlib-only, no imports beyond __future__. ADR-0017's require_compatible() gate does not exist in this file yet -- verified absent.

public_interface: window.STORY, window.ODYSSEY, window.DIFFS, window.ADRS, window.DIAGRAMS, window.DESIGNS (populated by sibling <script src> tags)
detail.rule: viewer/index.html never reaches into scripts/ (grep-verified: the one 'scripts/' mention is a code comment, not a live reference). It is not self-contained -- see CLAUDE.md 'The viewer is not self-contained' -- and depends on being served from the bundle root, a sibling of viewer/.

detail.note: Not yet a documented bounded context. Scripts write it, the viewer reads it; neither reads the other's source. Data-only, versioned by bundle.json / story.json meta.schema_version.
